preamble: Change of voiced /b/ to the voiceless bilabial fricative /ɸ/, combining spirantization and devoicing in a single step. The well-documented case is the Alor-Pantar language Teiwa, where non-initial Proto-Alor-Pantar *b weakened to a fricative (*haban > haɸan 'village') while initial *b was kept. A few Teiwa reflexes show voiced /v/ instead, and Holton & Robinson (2014) treat the split as unconditioned. Most other b > fricative changes produce voiced [β] or labiodental [f]/[v], so this exact outcome is rare.

examples.note: Medial *b weakened to a fricative in Teiwa and Nedebang (Nedebang afaŋ).
Same development of *b in word-final position after loss of the final vowel; initial *b is kept as /b/ in Teiwa.
Initial *b stays /b/ while the final *b becomes /ɸ/.

sources: Holton, G. & Robinson, L. C. (2014). The internal history of the Alor-Pantar language family. In M. Klamer (ed.), The Alor-Pantar languages: History and typology, 55–97. Berlin: Language Science Press. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.569388
